From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Lossless compression algorithm

 

This article is about the compression algorithm. For Brötli, the Swiss-German bread roll it is named after, see [Bread roll § Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread_roll#Europe "Bread roll").

__Brotli__ is a [lossless data compression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lossless_data_compression "Lossless data compression") algorithm developed by Jyrki Alakuijala and Zoltán Szabadka. It uses a combination of the general-purpose [LZ77](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LZ77_and_LZ78 "LZ77 and LZ78") lossless compression algorithm, [Huffman coding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huffman_coding "Huffman coding") and 2nd-order [context modelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Context_model "Context model"). Brotli is primarily used by [web servers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_servers "Web servers") and [content delivery networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_delivery_networks "Content delivery networks") to [compress HTTP content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_compression "HTTP compression"), making internet websites load faster. As successor to [gzip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gzip "Gzip"), it is supported by all major web browsers and has become increasingly popular, as it provides better compression than gzip.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-2)

## Name

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brotli&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Name")]

While Google's _[zopfli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zopfli "Zopfli")_ implementation of the deflate compression algorithm is named after Zöpfli, the [Swiss German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_German "Swiss German") word for a snack-sized [braided buttery bread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zopf "Zopf"), _brotli_ is named after Brötli, the Swiss German word for a [bread roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread_roll#Europe "Bread roll").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-intro-3)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brotli&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Google employees [Jyrki Alakuijala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jyrki_Alakuijala?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jyrki Alakuijala (page does not exist)") and Zoltán Szabadka developed Brotli in 2013 to decrease the size of [WOFF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_Open_Font_Format "Web Open Font Format") files.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-4) Alakuijala and Szabadka completed the Brotli specification during 2013–2016. The specification was accompanied with a reference implementation developed by two additional authors, Evgenii Kliuchnikov and Lode Vandevenne, who had previously developed Google's [zopfli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zopfli "Zopfli") implementation of [deflate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DEFLATE "DEFLATE") and [gzip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gzip "Gzip") compatible compression in 2013.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-comparison-5): 1 Unlike zopfli, which was a reimplementation of an existing data format specification, Brotli was a new data format and allowed the authors to improve compression ratios even further.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-intro-3)

The Brotli specification was generalized in September 2015 for HTTP stream compression (content-encoding type "br"). This generalized iteration also improved the compression ratio by using a predefined dictionary of frequently used words and phrases. The version of Brotli released in September 2015 by the Google software engineers contained enhancements in generic [lossless data compression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lossless_data_compression "Lossless data compression"), with particular emphasis on use for [HTTP compression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_compression "HTTP compression"). The encoder was partly rewritten, with the result that the compression ratio improved, both the encoder and the decoder have been sped up, the streaming API was improved, and more compression quality levels have been added. Additionally, the new release shows performance improvements across platforms, with decoding memory reduction.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-intro-3)

The [Internet Engineering Task Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_Engineering_Task_Force "Internet Engineering Task Force") approved the __Brotli compressed data format__ specification as an informational [request for comment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Request_for_Comments "Request for Comments") ([RFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RFC_(identifier) "RFC (identifier)") [7932](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7932)) in July 2016.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-ietf-6) The Brotli data format is an integral part of the 2nd iteration of the [Web Open Font Format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_Open_Font_Format "Web Open Font Format"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-ietf-6): 3 which was recognized in a 2021 Technology & Engineering Emmy Award from the [National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Television_Arts_&_Sciences "National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences") for font technology standardization at W3C.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-w3c_archive-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-w3c_emmy_press-8)

Brotli support has been added over the years to web browsers, with 96% of worldwide users using a browser that supports the format, as of July 2022.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-caniuse-9)

In 2016 [Dropbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dropbox "Dropbox") reimplemented Brotli in [Rust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language) "Rust (programming language)") to fulfill their requirement to be more secure against a malicious client.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-11)

## Algorithm

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brotli&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Algorithm")]

Brotli's new file format allows its authors to improve upon Deflate by several algorithmic and format-level improvements: the use of context models for literals and copy distances, describing copy distances through past distances, use of move-to-front queue in entropy code selection, joint-entropy coding of literal and copy lengths, the use of graph algorithms in block splitting, and a larger backward reference window are example improvements.

Unlike most general-purpose compression algorithms, Brotli uses a predefined dictionary, roughly 120 KiB in size, in addition to the dynamically populated ("sliding window") dictionary. The predefined dictionary contains over 13000 common words, phrases and other substrings derived from a large [corpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_corpus "Text corpus") of text and HTML documents.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-12)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-comparison-5) Using a predefined dictionary has been shown to increase compression where a file mostly contains commonly used words.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-13) Brotli's sliding window is limited to 16 [MiB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MiB "MiB"). This enables decoding on mobile phones with limited resources, but makes Brotli underperform on compression benchmarks having larger files. The constraints of the small window size can be alleviated by using _Large Window Brotli_, which is not compatible with RFC 7932 (Brotli proper).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-14)

## Implementations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brotli&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Implementations")]

Google's own implementation of the Brotli specification was released under the terms of the [permissive free software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permissive_free_software_license "Permissive free software license") [MIT license](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIT_license "MIT license") in 2016. A formal validation of the Brotli specification was independently implemented by [Mark Adler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Adler "Mark Adler"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-ietf-6): 126 one of the co-authors of the [zlib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlib "Zlib")/[gzip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gzip "Gzip") compression format and library. Adler's implementation was released under the terms of the similarly permissive [Apache License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache_License "Apache License").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-15) Other implementations of the specification also exist, including one in the source-to-source [Haxe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haxe "Haxe") language.

## Applications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brotli&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Applications")]

Brotli compression is generally used as an alternative to gzip on the web, as Brotli provides better overall compression.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-estimator-16) Compared to gzip compression, JavaScript files compressed with Brotli are roughly 15% smaller, HTML files are around 20% smaller, and CSS files are around 16% smaller.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-siteground-support-17)

The reference implementation does ship a command-line program `brotli` similar to `gzip`,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-18) but use in the Unix-like world as a simple compressor is scarce. [Libarchive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libarchive "Libarchive") developers find the raw stream format of `.br` files difficult to support, as there is no [magic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming) "Magic number (programming)") to indicate the file format.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-19)

## Industry support

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brotli&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Industry support")]

### Browsers and other clients

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brotli&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Browsers and other clients")]

* [Mozilla Firefox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mozilla_Firefox "Mozilla Firefox") introduced support for the "br" content-encoding method in version 44 (released on 26 January 2016).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-20)
* [Google Chrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Chrome "Google Chrome") has supported the "br" content-encoding method since version 50 (released on 20 April 2016).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-chromestatus-21)
* [Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opera_(web_browser) "Opera (web browser)") has supported the "br" content-encoding method since version 38 (released 8 June 2016).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-chromestatus-21)
* [Microsoft Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Edge "Microsoft Edge") has supported the "br" content-encoding method since version 15 (released on 5 April 2017).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-22)
* [Safari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safari_(web_browser) "Safari (web browser)") has supported the "br" content-encoding method since version 11 (released on 5 October 2017).
* [cURL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CURL "CURL") has a compile-time option to support the "br" content-encoding method using libbrotli as of version 7.57, released on 29 November 2017.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-23)
* [7zip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7zip "7zip") is available extended with Brotli by 7zip-zstd.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-24)
* [PeaZip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PeaZip "PeaZip") supports Brotli .BR format for compression and extraction[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-25)

### Web servers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brotli&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Web servers")]

* For [Apache HTTP Server](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache_HTTP_Server "Apache HTTP Server"), the "br" content-encoding method has been supported by the _[mod_brotli](https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/mod/mod_brotli.html)_ module since version 2.4.26.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-26)
* [Microsoft IIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_IIS "Microsoft IIS") has a supported extension since May 2018 that adds support for the "br" content-encoding method.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-27)
* [Microsoft Azure Front Door](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Azure "Microsoft Azure") can dynamically compress content on the edge using Brotli[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-28) since its launch on April 17, 2019.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-29)
* [nginx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nginx "Nginx") has a _[ngx_brotli](https://github.com/google/ngx_brotli)_ module provided by Google since December 2016.
* [Node.js](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node.js "Node.js") features a built-in native en- and decoder since version 11.7.0, which can be used to support the "br" content-encoding.
* [Amazon CloudFront](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_CloudFront "Amazon CloudFront") can automatically compress cacheable responses at the edge using Brotli, as of September 2020.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-30)
* [LiteSpeed Web Server](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LiteSpeed_Web_Server "LiteSpeed Web Server") has included the "br" content-encoding method for static files only since version 5.2 in July 2017.
* [Cloudflare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloudflare "Cloudflare") CDN offers a brotli option to compress data between its edge node and the user.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-31)
* [NaviServer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NaviServer "NaviServer") [added support](https://web.archive.org/web/20181101015345/https://bitbucket.org/naviserver/naviserver/src/tip/NEWS?at=default&fileviewer=file-view-default) in version 4.99.17b1
* [Caddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caddy_(web_server) "Caddy (web server)") serves statically compressed .br files since version 0.9.4 from December 21, 2016.
* [lighttpd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighttpd "Lighttpd") mod_deflate supports .br since 1.4.56[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brotli#cite_note-32) from November 2020.
